Lydia Park: Filing a small docs PR to add a 'debounced fallback' pattern to the error-ref page for 429s/timeouts/context limits. Idea: show a Ruby snippet, mention circuit-breaker style debounce to avoid thundering fallbacks, and a short migration blurb about Retry-After + canaries. @Samir @Roberta please review.

Samir V.: Love a Ruby examplewe don't have many. For debounce, suggest we show a basic in-memory counter with a short TTL and a note that customers should use a shared cache in multi-instance setups.

Roberta M.: Also call out 'context trim' naming and add an anchor to the err-ref. Linkcheck: one stale link to /old/batching -> replace with /docs/optimizations/batching.

Lydia Park: Draft Ruby snippet (very compact):

```ruby
# debounce fallback: simple counter with TTL
def generate_with_debounce(client, prompt)
  key = "fallback:#{prompt.hash}"
  count = $cache.get(key) || 0
  begin
    return client.text.generate(model: 'redwood-1', prompt: prompt)
  rescue => e
    status = e.respond_to?(:status) ? e.status : nil
    if status == 429
      $cache.set(key, count + 1, ttl: 30) if count < 5
      sleep((e.headers&.[]('Retry-After') || 1).to_i)
      # if count exceeded, go to lightweight model
      return client.text.generate(model: (count >= 5 ? 'redwood-1-small' : 'redwood-1'), prompt: prompt)
    end
    raise
  end
end
```

Samir V.: Nice. Add one-line comment about replacing $cache with Redis/Memcached in prod. Also shorten TTL suggestion to 15s in the snippet comments maybe.

Roberta M.: Migration blurb (short): "When upgrading, ensure clients honor Retry-After headers, prefer incremental backoff, and debounce fallbacks to avoid cascading loads. Normalize docs wording to 'context trim' and run small canary rollouts to validate behavior."
